title: The Star-Netter of Mirrormere
story: Every night, fallen star-sparks drift down onto Mirrormere lake, and every night Shimmerlurk scoops them up in her silver net. The lake spirits keep a ledger, and Shimmerlurk boasts she averaged exactly 24 sparks a night over the last five nights. Mr 6 reads the ledger: night one 18, night two 31, night three 26, night four 23 — and the fifth night's entry is smudged.
question: If Shimmerlurk's average really was 24 sparks per night over all five nights, how many sparks did she take on the fifth night?
solution: An average of 24 over 5 nights means the total was 24 × 5 = 120 sparks.
The four readable nights add to 18 + 31 + 26 + 23 = 98 sparks.
So the smudged night was 120 - 98 = 22 sparks.
praise: Adding up the four known nights was exactly right — the missing move was turning the average into a total first (24 × 5) and then subtracting.
hint: An average tells you the total in disguise: if five nights average 24, what do all five nights add up to?
victory: Mr 6 fills in the smudge with a flourish, and the ledger balances — Shimmerlurk must return all 120 sparks. She hands them back one by one, grumbling that she should have hired a better accountant.
imagePrompt: A glassy midnight lake reflecting falling star-sparks, a long elegant heron-like creature with a silver net recoiling as a small numeral '6' knight holds up a glowing ledger, cool blue-silver moonlight.
